transcript:
[2026-12-09 15:00:03] Meeting started. Duration: ~52 minutes.

Header: 2026-12-09 | 15:00 UTC | 52m
Attendees: Lina Park (Redwood AE), Owen Martinez (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Acuity Head of ML Ops), Jon Rivera (Acuity Platform Eng), Priya Desai (Acuity Security)

Auto-summary: Quick recap - we're scoping a POC to prove throughput and latency for Acuity's patient-summarization pipeline. Main asks: 1) integrate Acuity's test scripts into our benchmark harness; 2) run streaming and non-streaming scenarios; 3) define success criteria around p95 latency, errors, and throughput; 4) timeline to deliver initial benchmarks by 12/18.

Transcript:
[15:01] Lina Park: cool thanks everyone for joining, real quick agenda  benchmark harness integration, what your scripts look like, streaming vs non streaming, and timeline. owen's gonna walk through the harness.
[15:01] Owen Martinez: hey all, hi maya, jon, priya  quick note: our harness is a small repo with a runner, k6 load tests, and a streaming client; we support both gRPC streaming and rest streaming, though some of the jargon in traces we saw gets mis-transcribed sometimes, sorry, but we'll go slow. so first question, what does your customer script look like? is it single-shot prompts or long chit-chat sessions?
[15:02] Maya Singh: mostly single-shot summarizations but there are a subset where we stream partial notes from the EHR into the model and expect incremental outputs, so both. typical prompt lengths are about 350-600 tokens, occasionally up to 1.2k for complex encounters.
[15:03] Jon Rivera: and we run these at bursty times  for example morning syncs we'll see concurrent 120-200 reqs for a short window, sustained baseline is around 30-50 rps. we care about p95 latency under 750ms for non-streamed and p95 time-to-first-token under 250ms for streaming.
[15:03] Owen Martinez: good, that's helpful. for sizing we'll need sequence length distributions and expected concurrency; our harness can run k6 scenarios to simulate bursts and steady-state. question: do you plan to run the POC on Hosted API or Dedicated GPU pool or private VPC?
[15:04] Maya Singh: initial interest is Hosted to move fast, but if numbers don't meet cost/latency we may require Dedicated for predictable tail latency and isolation. security team will push for VPC/private eventually.
[15:04] Priya Desai: yep for compliance we need SOC2 evidence and ability to plug into our KMS for key management; also retention policies  can't store raw PHI beyond 30 days in any staging spaces.
[15:05] Lina Park: entirely reasonable. we'll send SOC2 + architecture docs. on KMS, our Private offering supports customer-managed keys; for Hosted we can discuss bring-your-own-key options, but we'll need to validate. owen, can the harness redact or mark PII in traces?
[15:05] Owen Martinez: the harness doesn't change payloads by default, but we have hooks where you can run a sanitizer function prior to sending. for the PO C let's keep the real prompts but we can run them in a test-only environ that we're guaranteed to purge; also we can provide guidance on tokenization and how to minimize exposure.
[15:06] Maya Singh: cool. on benchmarks, how do you handle streaming vs non-streaming fairness? we need apples-to-apples.
[15:06] Owen Martinez: good question  for streaming we measure two metrics: time-to-first-token (TTFT) and end-to-end completion time. for non-streaming we measure request latency and throughput. we'll run both with equivalent input sizes and concurrency patterns and look at p50/p95/p99. we also instrument token throughput and GPU utilization.
[15:08] Jon Rivera: what about KV cache and prefix caching? we rely on warm KV cache to speed follow-ups, but during initial cold starts it spikes latency.
[15:08] Owen Martinez: yep our runtime supports KV cache warmup scenarios; harness can simulate warm/cold by pre-warming sequences and then running the test. note that some transcriptions show K V cash  ha  but we know it's KV cache.
[15:09] Maya Singh: nice. about the harness integration  we have existing k6 scripts and a python runner that picks prompts from S3. can you ingest those as-is or do we need to refactor?
[15:09] Owen Martinez: we can ingest k6 pretty much as-is; for the python runner we have a shim that wraps their request shape. ideally you point us at a small sample repo, we drop a CI job in your pipeline, and run locally first. two ways: you hand us the scripts and we run them in our test account, or we give you the harness and instructions to run in your environment and post results back. both are fine.
[15:10] Priya Desai: security-wise we'd prefer to run the load tests from our environment to avoid sending PHI to external accounts. is that supported?
[15:10] Owen Martinez: yes  we support remote mode: the harness runs in your infra, hits Redwood endpoints; we provide a test API key and a read-only dashboard for result uploads. that keeps data stationary.
[15:11] Lina Park: perfect. success criteria  what would you consider a pass for this POC?
[15:11] Maya Singh: pass if p95 non-streamed latency < 750ms at 50 concurrency sustained, and streaming TTFT p95 < 250ms; error rate < 1% overall; also cost per 1k tokens within 20% of current budget estimate  though we can negotiate cost after we prove perf.
[15:12] Jon Rivera: and we want guidance on whether to run Dedicated vs Hosted given our workload; if Hosted meets targets at reasonable cost we avoid Dedicated procurement delays.
[15:12] Owen Martinez: ok we'll run Hosted first and produce a recommendation with cost curves and quantization tradeoffs. we'll test 8-bit quantized variants if you want lower cost paths, but we'd need to validate quality regressions.
[15:13] Priya Desai: about timelines  how long to get first benchmark numbers?
[15:13] Lina Park: if we get scripts and sample prompts this week, Owen can plug them in and run initial tests within 3 business days; then we'll do a follow-up review with results and any tuning. that puts initial numbers around 12/14-12/15. final POC report by 12/18.
[15:14] Maya Singh: that timeline works. one more question: streaming reliability  do you support partial retries if a chunk fails?
[15:15] Owen Martinez: we have idempotency keys and chunk-level ack patterns in our streaming layer; retries are possible but you'll see variability in TTFT for retries. the harness can flip retries on/off to measure impact.
[15:16] Jon Rivera: for load profile, can you simulate our morning burst pattern? it's ~180 concurrent for 5-8 minutes then back to baseline.
[15:16] Owen Martinez: yes, we can set up a mixed scenario: ramp to 200 conc in 30s, sustain 8m, then drop to 40 rps for 30m. we'll capture GPU utilization and queue depth metrics.
[15:17] Maya Singh: note our tokens per request vary  we will provide distribution with percentiles  10/50/90/99 for token lengths.
[15:18] Lina Park: great. any blockers from procurement or security?
[15:18] Priya Desai: procurement will need standard MSA language and data processing addendum; also we need the SOC2 report and an architecture diagram for VPC peering. I'll review the compliance packet once you send it.
[15:19] Lina Park: will do; I'll send SOC2 + VPC diagram and a pointer to how BYOK works for our Private offering.
[15:19] Owen Martinez: also sending an example k6 script and the harness repo link. we'll include a README with instructions for running the test locally in your VPC.
[15:20] Maya Singh: who on your side will own running the first test vs us running it in our infra?
[15:20] Lina Park: Owen will run initial tests in Redwood-hosted test account if you prefer a quick start, but since you flagged PHI, we'll default to giving you the harness to run in your account. Owen can run parity tests in our test account with scrubbed prompts.
[15:21] Jon Rivera: ok we'll run it in our account, but will need the shim and an example CI job. we'll also need temporary test creds for a dev endpoint.
[15:21] Owen Martinez: we'll provide dev/test creds with limited TTL and RBAC. after your run, you can upload results to our dashboard or share logs securely.
[15:22] Lina Park: recap  acquir: (sic) acuity provide prompts and token distribution by 12/13; owen provides harness and k6 examples by 12/11; priya to review compliance packet by 12/10; schedule workshop by 12/14. initial numbers targeted for 12/15, final report by 12/18. anyone want to change anything?
[15:23] Maya Singh: no, that sounds good. thanks everyone.
[15:25] Meeting ended.

Notes: Transcript includes a few mis-typed terms (K V cash = KV cache; POC spelled variations). Some speakers labeled generically in auto-transcript system but corrected above.

References shared during call: - Redwood harness repo (link to be sent) - Example k6 scripts (attached) - SOC2 + VPC architecture doc (to be sent)

End of transcript.
